contract: Read the first packet before each backward seek and compare the landed video position and complete packet suffix.
Source sync seeks use sample composition time and demux seeks use the projected video clock. The reference seeks backward in the public MOV demux clock.
Compare track, PTS, DTS, duration, flags, size, payload, position, time base and encoded trim. Preserve every original range case, including start-up and Opus roll recovery.
For range playback compare the presentation duration in microseconds. Release seek checkpoints before the checkpoint control and compare the resulting seek.
Preload input outside the measurement window.

pending_module_requirements: Compare source composition time, sync samples and the secondary-track prefix under ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.6.1 and 8.6.2. The source seek and FFmpeg's demux-clock seek can land at different samples or retain different preroll.

Compare the presentation extent in the movie and track declarations under ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.2 and 8.6 with AVFormatContext.duration after stream discovery. Both readers deliver packets but report different presentation durations.
Check source sync signalling against demux flags under ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.6.1 and 8.6.2. The AV1 sample extents and clocks match, while the reference marks a packet disposable.
Check MOV edit-list and track admission under ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.3 and 8.6. The candidate rejects a plan or seek which the public MOV demuxer accepts.

Compare edit-list occurrence order, duration and encoded trim under ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.6. The demux seek lands and returns packets, but the selected suffix, edit endpoint or skip-samples side data differs.
Check the first eligible sync sample under ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.6.2. The source seek refuses with no preceding sync in the target configuration while the reference emits packets.
Verify the empty edit under ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.6.6. The movie seek reports an empty mapping and emits no packets, while FFmpeg's demux seek falls back to media.
Check the movie-to-media edit mapping under ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.6.6. Movie seek applies the mapped request and replays source state, while FFmpeg starts a demux packet suffix.
